transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-19
Start: 15:17 UTC
Duration: 55 mins (approx)
Attendees: Lauren Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nambiar (Monarch Head of ML), Ethan Zhou (Head of Platform), Maria Lopez (Procurement)

Summary: quick renewal check-in with decision to add EU on-prem pilot to contract; discussed capacity uplift, timeline for staging and SOC2 artifacts, and fallback policies. Agreed to updated amendment and pilot kickoff next week.

Links referenced: https://redwood.example.com/procure/quote-DEAL-82931 (quoted spreadsheet), private-runbook-v1.pdf (upload pending), SOC2-summary.pdf (customer to share)

Transcript:
[00:00] Lauren: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I realize it's end of week for some so we'll try to keep this tight. goal for today is a renewal readout and lock the EU on-prem activation date.
[00:12] Priya: yeah thanks Lauren. we got the renewal terms last week, Maria's been gonna review but first we need clarity on the on-prem footprint and whether the dedicated capacity uplift will cover our peak batch jobs.
[00:25] Diego: got it. quick note, when we say on-prem here we mean Redwood Private with customer-managed control plane in the EU region — small distinction from a hosted dedicated node. that means we ship the control plane and the inference runtime runs in your VPC or on-prem nodes.
[00:40] Ethan: yeah that's what we need, because of data residency and the regulator. just to be clear: we're looking at an initial 20 GPU-equivalent reserved capacity with burst to 30 for seasonal spikes — is that what you modeled?
[00:52] Lauren: correct. in the quote i modeled 20 reserved, 10 burst credits, and a short pilot for the first 4 weeks at a reduced rate, then full commit on 2027-09-01. we can shift dates if you need.
[01:05] Maria: procurement question — does the amendment change invoicing terms? we prefer monthly invoice consolidated across hosted and private.
[01:12] Lauren: good question. the amendment will list private deployment as an addendum; billing can remain consolidated monthly. the main difference is a one-time activation fee for the private control plane. i'll mark that clearly in the quote.
[01:25] Priya: Diego, on the tech side, we need to validate latency for our 8k sequence gen baseline and cold-start behavior for request volumes. can you run a quick benchmark during the pilot?
[01:35] Diego: absolutely. we'll run the 8k seqs, the continuous-batching pattern you described, and measure tail latency at p95/p99. i can also include KV cache warm-up curves. caveat: the first 48 hours will show higher cold-starts until caches warm.
[01:50] Ethan: and what about model variants? we might want a smaller quantized variant for lower-cost paths. does Redwood support automated fallback from the production model to a quantized replica when capacity is constrained?
[02:02] Diego: yes — routing policies can fall back to a compatible quantized variant. we'll show the routing policy config during the pilot. keep in mind quality differences; we'll include quality delta numbers in the runbook.
[02:15] Priya: perfect. also, security — SOC2 and KMS. we have a phishing audit coming and need KMS integration with our HSM. can Redwood's private offering plug into customer-managed KMS?
[02:27] Lauren: yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations. Diego can sketch the keyflow for you. we'll also attach our SOC2 summary in the amendment, but Maria will still need your full report copy.
[02:40] Maria: yes, procurement needs that for the file before legal signs. timeline: we need vendor SOC2 artifacts by next week to move things along.
[02:48] Diego: noted. i'll ask our security team to produce a redactable SOC2 package, and i'll include a runbook diagram of key lifecycle, and where encryption in transit vs at rest sits.
[03:02] Priya: regarding rollout — pilot steps? we want staging, soak, then canary to prod. what is typical cadence?
[03:12] Diego: typical is: week 0 — install control plane in staging, week 1 — ingest sample traffic and run benchmarks, week 2 — soak and validate QoS and cost telemetry, week 3 — UAT with limited users and canary routing, week 4 — handover and scale to reserved capacity if metrics meet agreed SLOs. we can compress that if you want a faster ramp.
[03:35] Ethan: i think we need two weeks minimum in staging because of firewall and network approvals. also want a dry run of failover to hosted fallback in case on-prem nodes degrade.
[03:45] Lauren: absolutely, fallback policy will allow traffic to redirect to hosted dedicated nodes in the eu region if the private cluster has issues; Diego will configure automatic failover thresholds.
[03:56] Priya: are there limits on tokenization or function calling with private runtime? we call a lot of tools and chain outputs.
[04:05] Diego: function/tool calling is supported but depends on outbound network rules; we need your egress patterns. also streaming is supported, but we need to align on session pinning if you do long-lived chats.
[04:20] Maria: timeline again from procurement: can we get the final amendment by friday 2027-07-22? legal review is tight.
[04:28] Lauren: yes that's the ask we'll hit. i'll include separate line items: reserved capacity, burst credits, activation fee, and professional services for the private install.
[04:40] Priya: on sizing, one more ask: show us the cost delta between keeping everything hosted vs the hybrid approach — specifically impact on per-1k-token cost at p50/p95.
[04:52] Diego: will do. i'll produce a two-sheet estimate: per-token economics with quantized fallback and one with full fp16 models. should help you pick the tradeoff.
[05:05] Ethan: also, we may need to run a benchmark against our existing vendor, CloudModelCo, to justify migration. is Redwood open to running a side-by-side on our infra during the pilot?
[05:16] Lauren: yes. we'll coordinate a controlled bench; note that results depend heavily on model variant and kernel selection. we'll include a reproducible script so the bench is apples-to-apples.
[05:30] Priya: ok great. any blockers from Redwood's side for starting week of 2027-07-26?
[05:37] Diego: only thing we need is a staging VPC with network peering enabled and some test keys. and access to a SOC2 contact for artifact exchange.
[05:46] Maria: i'll get you the contact and start the procurement paperwork once i have the amendment.
[05:52] Lauren: perfect. let's recap next steps — i'll send the amendment and pricing (Lauren), Diego will upload runbook and bench script and record a short demo (Diego), Priya will circulate compliance contact and expected policies (Priya), Ethan will confirm IP allowlist and staging windows (Ethan). kickoff call scheduled tentatively for 2027-07-27 09:00 UTC pending paperwork.
[06:17] Priya: sounds good. small note — on SLA, we need to see p99 < 1200ms for our interactive flows; will that be reasonable?
[06:27] Diego: we'll target that in the pilot. depending on model size and pooling, p99 for the quantized fallback should be under 1s, and the full model p99 might be around 1.1s in your eu on-prem profile — but we'll verify.
[06:43] Maria: last procurement Q: is there an option to cap monthly spend if we hit unexpected usage?
[06:50] Lauren: yes we can include usage alerts and a soft cap, and then an operations contact will engage. we'll add that in the amendment.
[07:02] Ethan: ok thank you everyone.
[07:05] Lauren: thanks all, i'll follow up with notes and the doc links. end meeting.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribution (speaker times approximate), some technical acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., KV cache spelled "k-v cache"), natural speech pauses and interruptions preserved.
